mainTopic: How a גט reaches the wife: her bed and basket in his house, telling her 'Here is your גט', her slave, and throwing it in a public area
overview: This amud finishes the rule that a raised spot in the courtyard with its own name counts as a separate place. It then asks when a גט thrown to a wife inside her husband's house works. If it lands on her own bed, the bed must be ten טפחים high. If it lands in her basket, several אמוראים explain the case, and רבי יוחנן says the spot of her lap and basket is hers because the husband does not care about it. A new משנה teaches that a גט she received as a loan document, found behind him, or got while asleep works only once he says 'Here is your גט'. The גמרא explains that she must have pulled it from him while he leaned toward her. A ברייתא shows רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר arguing about these cases. רבא rules on a גט placed in the hand of her sleeping slave, and the גמרא limits this to a slave who is tied up. A last משנה deals with a גט thrown to her in a public area, and the גמרא begins defining 'closer to her' and 'halfway'. רב כהנא's explanation of 'halfway' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A raised spot with its own name counts as a separate place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. If the raised area has its own special name, it is a separate place even if it is not 10 טפחים high or 4 אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: …a special name. But if it does have a special name, then even though it is not ten handbreadths high, and even though it is not four cubits, it counts as a separate place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a discussion from the previous page about a raised area in the courtyard. It finishes the rule: what matters is whether people call that spot by its own name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a spot counts as its own area only if it is high enough or big enough. Here the גמרא adds that a שם לוואי, a special name, is enough by itself. Once people name it separately, it is treated as a separate place, so a גט landing there does not count as landing in her area.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'side name': a special name that sets a place apart from what is around it
Ten (טפחים, handbreadths): the usual height that makes a separate area
Four cubits: the usual minimum size for a separate area

steps.whatToRemember: A name can make a place separate, even when its size or height alone would not.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The first half of it is on the previous page.

phrases.english: …a special name;
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: we only said this when the spot has no special name.

phrases.english: but if it has a special name –

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: even though it is not ten high,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: and even though it is not four cubits, it is a separate place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion carried over from the previous page
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A spot with its own name is a separate area, whatever its height or size.

steps.title: רבא: the bed rule applies only to the husband's bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a גט thrown onto the bed. רבא limits it: she is not divorced only if it is his bed. If it is her bed, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'even if it is with her in the bed, etc.' רבא said: They only taught this about his bed. But in her bed, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. רבא then explains exactly when that line applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a גט thrown to her inside his house does not work, even if it lands on the bed with her. רבא says this is because the bed belongs to him, so the גט never reached her property. If the bed is hers, the גט has landed in something of hers, so she is divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about…: a phrase that limits a rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole discussion that follows: can something she owns acquire the גט for her while it sits in his house?

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'Even if it is with her in the bed, etc.'
phrases.notes: 'It' here means the גט, which landed on the bed where she is.

phrases.english: רבא said:
They only taught this about his bed;
but in her bed, she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא לא שנו אלא במטה שלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case where she is not divorced is when the bed is his. A גט that lands on her own bed divorces her.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying the same thing as רבא: in his bed she is not divorced, and in her bed she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says: in his bed, she is not divorced; in her bed, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's limit on the משנה is now backed by an older source. רבי אליעזר makes the same split between his bed and her bed. So רבא's distinction is not just his own idea.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way: a ברייתא that supports what was just said

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
רבי אליעזר says:
in his bed – she is not divorced;
in her bed – she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's statement
steps.raayaObject: רבא's split between his bed and her bed

steps.title: Her bed is like a buyer's vessel in the seller's property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can her bed acquire the גט when it stands in his house? That is like a buyer's vessel in the seller's property. Can we really learn from here that such a vessel acquires for the buyer?
steps.simpleTranslation: And in her bed she is divorced? But that is a buyer's vessel in the seller's property! Can you learn from this that a buyer's vessel in the seller's property acquires for the buyer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא and the ברייתא. It also asks whether this case proves a rule that is argued about elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her bed belongs to her, but it is standing in his house. That is just like a buyer whose vessel sits in the seller's property, and it is not clear such a vessel acquires anything for its owner. If she is divorced here, it seems to prove that it does, and the גמרא questions whether we can say that.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel or container. A person's vessel can acquire items placed into it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the roles. The wife is like the 'buyer', because she is the one receiving the גט. The husband is like the 'seller', because the bed stands in his house.

phrases.english: And in her bed – she is divorced?

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר הוּא;
phrases.english: It is a buyer's vessel in the seller's property!
phrases.notes: Her bed is her 'vessel', and it is standing in her husband's house.

phrases.english: Can you learn from this

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר – קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ?
phrases.english: that when a buyer's vessel is in the seller's property, the buyer acquires?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling that רבא and the ברייתא agreed on
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a גט landing on her bed divorces her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her bed stands in his house, so it is like a buyer's vessel in the seller's property. It is questionable whether such a vessel acquires, so it should not be able to acquire the גט for her.

steps.title: The bed is ten handbreadths high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא and רבי אליעזר are talking about a bed that is 10 טפחים high, so it counts as its own area.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, this is needed for a case where the bed is ten handbreadths high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. Her bed is tall enough to count as a separate area, so it is not inside his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that her bed is just her vessel sitting in his house. A surface 10 טפחים high is treated as its own area. So the גט lands in her area, not in his house.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case (it is talking about a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed where it is ten high.
phrases.notes: 'Ten' means ten טפחים, which is enough height to make the bed its own separate area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her bed is just her vessel standing in his house, so it should not acquire for her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bed is 10 טפחים high, so it is a separate area and not part of his house.

steps.title: But the bed's legs stand on his floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even a tall bed has legs that rest on the husband's floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the place of the legs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The bed's legs stand on his floor, so the bed is still resting in his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Height alone may not be enough. The bed still stands on ground that belongs to him. So maybe it is still inside his property after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the legs stand

phrases.english: But there is the place of the legs!
phrases.notes: He means the spots on the husband's floor where the bed's legs rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a 10 טפחים bed is fully separate from his house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The legs rest on his floor, so the bed is still standing in his property.

steps.title: People do not care about the spot under the legs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people are not particular about the tiny spot under a bed's legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: People are not particular about the place of the legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the space under the legs is so small that the husband does not care about it, so it does not make the bed part of his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the owner does not mind that small spot, it is as if it is not really his for this purpose. So the tall bed stays her own separate area, and the גט she gets on it divorces her.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not particular / do not mind

steps.whatToRemember: Her bed works only if it is 10 טפחים high, and the spot under its legs does not count, because people do not care about it.

phrases.english: About the place of the legs
people are not particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and closes the bed discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the problem is not important
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The legs on his floor make the bed part of his property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nobody cares about such a small spot, so the bed stays her separate area.

steps.title: The same problem with her basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a גט thrown into her lap or basket divorces her, and asks: her basket in his house is a buyer's vessel in the seller's property!
steps.simpleTranslation: Into her lap or into her basket, she is divorced. Why? It is the buyer's vessel in the seller's property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the next line of the משנה, about her lap or basket. It asks the same kind of question it asked about the bed in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a גט thrown into her lap or basket divorces her, even though she is in his house. But her basket is an object of hers sitting in his house. That looks like a buyer's vessel in the seller's property, which may not acquire for the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: The buyer's vessel in the seller's property

phrases.english: Into her lap or into her basket –
she is divorced. Why?

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר הוּא!
phrases.english: It is the buyer's vessel in the seller's property!
phrases.notes: Here the wife is like the 'buyer' getting the גט, and the husband is like the 'seller' whose house it is in.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְתוֹךְ חֵיקָהּ אוֹ לְתוֹךְ קַלְתָּהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of question as step 4, now on the basket case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a גט thrown into her basket divorces her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The basket is her vessel standing in his property, which may not acquire for her.

steps.title: The basket was hanging from her
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, and also רבי אושעיא, explain that the basket was hanging from her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is a case where her basket was hanging from her. And so said רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא: it is a case where her basket was hanging from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a basket hanging on her. Two separate chains of teachers say the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket hanging from her body is attached to her, not resting in his house. So it is like her own body, and the גט reaches her directly.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / it is a case where
And so said (another teacher says the same)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Such as where her basket was hanging from her.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Elazar that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Such as where her basket was hanging from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her basket is resting in his house like a buyer's vessel in the seller's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket hangs from her body, so it is not resting in his property at all.

steps.title: Tied to her is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says the basket only needs to be tied to her, even if it is not hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: tied, even though it is not hanging.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a wider answer: as long as the basket is tied to her, it is enough, even if it is resting on the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, being tied to her is enough of a connection to make it hers and not part of his house. So he allows more cases than שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though it is not hanging

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: קְשׁוּרָה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: tied,
even though it is not hanging.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר קְשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a wider answer than step 9 to the same challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It must hang from her body.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being tied to her is enough, even if it does not hang.

steps.title: The basket was between her thighs
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the basket was resting between her thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: it is a case where her basket was placed between her thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a different answer: the basket was lying right between her legs where she sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basket is in the very spot where she is sitting. The husband does not mind the place where she sits, so that spot counts as hers. So the basket is in her area.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Such as where her basket was placed for her
between her thighs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה קַלְתָּהּ מוּנַּחַת לָהּ בֵּין יַרְכוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The basket is resting in his property.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is in the place where she sits, which the husband does not mind, so it is her area.

steps.title: Her husband sells baskets
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא בר רב דימי says the husband was a basket seller, so he does not care where a basket lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא בר רב דימי said: it is a case where her husband sold baskets.
steps.whatsHappening: A last answer: the husband is a basket seller. His place is full of baskets, so he does not care about the spot where her basket sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as the bed legs in step 7: if the owner does not care about a spot, it does not count as his. So her basket is in her own area and the גט divorces her.
steps.whatToRemember: All the answers show the basket is not truly 'in his property': it hangs from her, is tied to her, sits between her thighs, or lies where the husband does not care.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בַּר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya bar Rav Dimi said:
Such as where her husband was a seller of baskets.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בַּר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ מוֹכֵר קְלָתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The basket rests in his property, so it cannot acquire for her.
steps.terutzMaskana: A basket seller does not care where a basket lies, so that spot counts as her area.

steps.title: The spot of her lap and basket belongs to her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the question about her basket in his house differently: the place where her lap and her basket rest is considered hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: The place of her lap belongs to her, and the place of her basket belongs to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives another answer to the question from Step 8. He says no special setup is needed, because the spot under her lap and under her basket already counts as hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers made the basket count as hers by limiting the case: hanging from her, tied to her, between her thighs, or a husband who sells baskets. רבי יוחנן avoids all of that. He says the ground under the basket itself belongs to her, so the basket is not resting in the seller's property at all.

keyTerms.meaning: belongs to her, is owned by her

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer works for an ordinary basket lying anywhere in the house, so the משנה can be read as written without having to limit the case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
the place of her lap belongs to her,
the place of her basket belongs to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מְקוֹם חֵיקָהּ קָנוּי לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth answer to the question in Step 8, broader than the answers in Steps 9-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines who owns the location: the spot itself is hers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The basket sits in the husband's property, so whatever is in it is in the seller's domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The place of her lap and basket is considered hers, so the גט lands in her own domain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place of a wife's lap and basket belongs to her.

steps.title: Why those spots are hers
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבי יוחנן's reason: a husband does not care about the place of his wife's lap or basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי יוחנן's reason? Because a person does not care about the place of her lap or the place of her basket.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks why רבי יוחנן says those spots belong to her, and then answers his own question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband does not mind his wife using those small spots, so it is as if he gave them to her. This explains how a place in his house can count as her property.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan?
Because a person is not particular
not about the place of her lap
nor about the place of her basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the husband does not care about these spots, it is as if he gave them to her.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a גט thrown into her lap, her basket, or anything like her basket divorces her, which matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If he threw it into her lap, or into her basket, or into anything like her basket, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not limit the case to a basket that is hanging or tied. It even adds 'anything like her basket,' which fits רבי יוחנן's idea that the spot of such items is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)

phrases.english: This is also taught:
if he threw it to her into her lap
or into her basket,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְתוֹךְ כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא כְּקַלְתָּהּ –
phrases.english: or into anything that is like her basket –
then she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that the place of her lap and basket belongs to her.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that validates a גט thrown into her lap, basket, or anything like her basket, without requiring the basket to hang or be tied.

steps.title: What does 'anything like her basket' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra item the ברייתא means to include with the words 'anything like her basket.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anything that is like her basket' — what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the extra wording in the ברייתא and asks what it adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said 'her basket.' Adding 'anything like her basket' must be there to include some other item, so the גמרא wants to know which one.

phrases.english: 'Anything that is like her basket' –
what does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא כְּקַלְתָּהּ – לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ברייתא from Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which additional item the phrase 'anything like her basket' includes.

steps.title: It includes her date basket
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes the small basket she eats dates from, since the husband does not care about its place either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the basket she eats dates from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra wording includes the little basket she eats dates from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like her work basket, this is a personal item whose spot the husband does not care about. So a גט thrown into it also lands in her domain.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the spot of a wife's lap, her basket, and similar personal items like her date basket counts as hers. A גט thrown there divorces her even in his house, because he does not care about those spots.

phrases.english: to include the basket
from which she eats dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes the small basket she eats dates from.

steps.title: A גט handed over as a loan document does not count
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that if the husband calls the גט a loan document, or she finds it behind him and reads it, it is not a valid גט until he says, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to her, 'Take this loan document,' or she found it behind him, and she reads it and sees it is her גט, it is not a גט until he says to her, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what the husband must say when giving the גט. If she does not receive it as a גט, the divorce does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the paper itself really is a גט, but she did not receive it as one. Either he called it a loan document, or she simply found it. The משנה says the divorce works only once he tells her, 'Here is your גט.'

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not how the גט is written. The paper is a proper גט. The problem is how it was given: she has to receive it as a גט.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he said to her:
'Take this promissory note,'
phrases.notes: The paper is really a גט, but he tells her it is a loan document.

phrases.english: or she found it behind him,
she reads it and it is her bill of divorce –
it is not a valid bill of divorce,
until he says to her: 'This is your bill of divorce.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ: כִּנְסִי שְׁטַר חוֹב זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic after the basket discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given as something else, or found by her, is not valid until the husband tells her, 'Here is your גט.'

steps.title: The sleeping wife: a גט placed in her hand while she sleeps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a case: if the husband put the גט in his sleeping wife's hand, and she wakes up, reads it, and sees it is her גט, it is not valid until he says, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put it in her hand while she was asleep, and she woke up, read it, and saw it was her גט, it is not a valid גט until he says to her, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases where the husband did not properly tell his wife what he was giving her. Here she was asleep when the גט was put in her hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט did physically reach her hand, but she was asleep and did not know what she was receiving. So it does not work until he tells her clearly, 'Here is your גט.' This matches the earlier cases in the same משנה (the 'loan document' case and the 'found behind him' case).

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here is your גט': the words the husband must say

phrases.english: If he put it in her hand while she was sleeping;
she woke up, she reads it,
and behold, it is her גט:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גֵּט, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהּ ״הֵא גִּיטִּיךְ״.
phrases.english: it is not a valid גט until he says to her, 'Here is your גט.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 18 with one more case that follows the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט put in a sleeping woman's hand is not valid until the husband tells her, 'Here is your גט.'

steps.title: Saying 'Here is your גט' should not help when she found it behind him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in the case where she found the גט behind him, how do his words fix anything? It is like telling her to pick it up from the ground, and רבא rules that such words do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he says to her, 'Here is your גט,' what does that accomplish? It is like saying, 'Take your גט off the ground.' And רבא said that if a man says 'Take your גט off the ground,' he has said nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case from step 18, where the wife found the גט lying behind her husband. It asks how his saying 'Here is your גט' can make it valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט only works if the husband gives it to her. If the גט is just lying behind him and she picks it up, he never handed it over. His words are no better than telling her to take it off the floor, and רבא says that does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it accomplish? What of it?
He said nothing; it has no effect

steps.confusionAlert: The question is about the 'found behind him' case, not the sleeping case. In the sleeping case the גט was really placed in her hand.

phrases.english: GEMARA: When he says to her, 'Here is your גט,'
what does that accomplish?

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ ״טְלִי גִּיטִּיךְ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע״,
phrases.english: It is like saying, 'Take your גט off the ground,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: ״טְלִי גִּיטִּיךְ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע״ –
phrases.english: and רבא said: 'Take your גט off the ground':
he has said nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר לַהּ הֵא גִּיטִּיךְ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'found behind him' ruling from the משנה in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a גט found behind the husband becomes valid once he says 'Here is your גט.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He never handed her the גט, so this is like telling her to take it off the ground, which רבא says has no effect.

steps.title: She pulled it out from behind him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the גט was not lying on the ground. It was on the husband's body, and she pulled it out from behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that she pulled it out from behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's case differently. The גט was on him, and she pulled it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גט was attached to the husband, for example tucked in his belt, it is not like a גט lying on the ground. It comes to her from his own body, so his words 'Here is your גט' can count.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read the case this way

phrases.english: Say: it means she pulled it out from behind him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט was lying on the ground behind him, so it was never given by him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט was on his body, and she pulled it from behind him.

steps.title: Pulling it out still is not the husband giving it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even if she pulled it out, the תורה says the husband must give the גט into her hand, and here she took it herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if she pulled it out, there is still a problem: we need 'and he shall put it in her hand,' and that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 21, saying that her pulling it out does not fix the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the husband to actively give the גט. If she pulls it out by herself, she is the one acting, not him. So the גט should still be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall put it in her hand': the פסוק's requirement that he give it
It is missing; it is not here

phrases.english: If she pulled it out, that is also a problem,
since we need 'and he shall put it in her hand,' and that is missing!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלָפַתּוּ נָמֵי הָא בָּעֵינָא וְנָתַן בְּיָדָהּ וְלֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that she pulled the גט out from behind him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires the husband to give the גט; if she takes it herself, he did not give it.

steps.title: He bent his waist toward her and she pulled it out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the husband bent his waist toward her and she pulled the גט out. His leaning toward her counts as his giving it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where he bent his waist toward her and she pulled it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer, narrowing the case so that the husband does play an active part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By leaning his waist, where the גט is tucked, toward her, the husband brings the גט to her himself. That counts as 'he shall put it in her hand,' even though she did the final pulling. Then his words 'Here is your גט' complete the divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: A גט found behind the husband works only if it was on his body and he leaned toward her so she could pull it out, and then he says 'Here is your גט.' The husband must always be the one giving.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously the תורה's rule that the husband gives the גט is taken. Even a small act, like leaning toward her, is needed to count as his giving.

phrases.english: No, the case is needed
where he bent his waist toward her, and she pulled it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דַּעֲרַק לַהּ חַרְצֵיהּ וּשְׁלַפְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22 by making the case narrower.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She pulled the גט out by herself, so he did not give it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He bent his waist toward her, so it is as if he gave it into her hand.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the משנה: loan document or pulled from behind
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling as the משנה. If the husband called the גט a loan document, or she pulled it from behind him, it is not a גט until he says 'Here is your גט.' That is רבי's view. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires him to take it back and give it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא. Suppose he said to her, 'Take this loan document,' or she pulled it out from behind him. She read it, and it turned out to be her גט. It is not a valid גט until he says to her, 'Here is your גט.' These are the words of רבי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: it is never a גט until he takes it from her, gives it to her again, and says to her, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as our משנה, to back it up. The ברייתא also adds a second opinion, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי, like the משנה, holds that the husband's words 'Here is your גט' are enough to fix the problem, even though she already has the paper. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that words alone are not enough. The גט must actually be handed to her again, this time as a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put together the משנה. His opinion matches the unnamed משנה, which is why this ברייתא supports it.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
If he said to her, 'Take this loan document,'
or she pulled it out from behind him,
and she read it, and it turned out to be her bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גֵּט, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהּ ״הֵא גִּיטִּיךְ״,
phrases.english: it is not a valid bill of divorce until he says to her, 'Here is your bill of divorce,'
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
It is never a valid bill of divorce
until he takes it from her,
and then gives it to her again,
and says to her, 'Here is your bill of divorce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the משנה's ruling, as explained in steps 20 to 23, with a ברייתא that teaches the same case.
steps.raayaObject: The reading from step 21 that the משנה's case is שלפתו מאחוריו (she pulled it out from behind him), which the ברייתא states outright, along with the ruling that it works once he says 'Here is your גט.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) that says this in the name of רבי.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: the sleeping wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's second case: he put the גט in her hand while she slept. רבי says it works once he says 'Here is your גט.' רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says he must take it back and give it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put it in her hand while she was sleeping, and she woke up, read it, and it turned out to be her גט, it is not a גט until he says to her, 'Here is your גט.' These are the words of רבי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: not until he takes it from her, gives it to her again, and says to her, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with a second case, the sleeping wife from our משנה. The same two opinions argue the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that she was asleep when the גט was put in her hand. Even so, רבי still says words afterward are enough. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר still says it must be handed over again.

phrases.english: If he put it in her hand while she was sleeping,
and she woke up and read it, and it turned out to be her bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גֵּט, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהּ: ״הֵא גִּיטִּיךְ״,
phrases.english: it is not a valid bill of divorce until he says to her, 'Here is your bill of divorce,'
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Not until he takes it from her,
and then gives it to her again,
and says to her, 'Here is your bill of divorce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the second case, which matches step 19 in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping wife: רבי says saying 'Here is your גט' afterward is enough. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says he must take it back and hand it over again.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: we might think רבי agrees in the sleeping case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא repeats the argument. If we only had the first case, we might say רבי is lenient there only because she was awake and fit to be divorced. In the sleeping case, we might think he agrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both cases are needed. If the argument were stated only in the first case, we would say רבי holds his view there because she is fit to be divorced. But if he put it in her hand while she was sleeping, she is not fit to be divorced. So we might say that there רבי agrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: why does the ברייתא repeat the same argument twice? This step gives the first half of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she was awake, she was able to receive a גט at the moment she got the paper, so words added later might be enough. When she was asleep, she could not receive a גט at all at that moment, so we might think רבי would also require a new handing over. The sleeping case teaches that רבי is lenient even there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (both cases have to be taught)
Fit to be divorced, able to receive a גט at that moment
I would say (what we might have mistakenly thought)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אֵימָא מוֹדֵי' is only what we might have thought. It is not the real הלכה. The ברייתא teaches that רבי does argue in the sleeping case too.

phrases.english: And both cases are needed;
for if it were stated only in the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is 'loan document' or 'pulled from behind', where she was awake.

phrases.english: we would say that in that case Rabbi holds his view
because she is fit to be divorced;
but if he put it in her hand while she was sleeping,
where she is not fit to be divorced,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר;
phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא in steps 24 and 25 repeats the same argument in both cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the awake case, רבי might agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר when she was asleep, since then she could not be divorced at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sleeping case is needed to show that רבי is lenient even there.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: we might think רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees in the awake case
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the sleeping case, we might think רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict only there and agrees with רבי in the awake case. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the argument were stated only in this case, the sleeping wife, we would say that only here רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds his view. But in the other case, I would say he agrees with רבי. So both cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of its explanation and finishes by saying again that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sleeping case is the weaker one, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's strictness there would not teach us much. The awake case is needed to show that he is strict even when she was able to be divorced. Each case teaches the strength of a different opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי says that saying 'Here is your גט' afterward is enough, even if she was asleep when she got it. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it must be handed over again, even if she was awake. That is why the ברייתא teaches both cases.

phrases.english: And if it were stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' means the sleeping wife, the one just mentioned.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר;
phrases.english: we would say that only in this case Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds his view;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ – אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי;
phrases.english: but in the other case, I would say he agrees with Rabbi;
so both cases are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא from step 26 by explaining the other direction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed. The awake case shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is strict even there, and the sleeping case shows that רבי is lenient even there.

steps.title: רבא: A גט placed in the hand of her sleeping slave
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a גט placed in the hand of the wife's sleeping slave, whom she is watching, is a valid גט. If the slave is awake, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If a man wrote a גט for his wife and put it in the hand of her slave while the slave was asleep and she was watching over him, it is a valid גט. If the slave was awake, it is not a גט, because then he is like a courtyard that is guarded without her awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא about giving a גט by placing it in the hand of the wife's slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman's slave belongs to her, like her courtyard, and a courtyard can acquire a גט for its owner. When the slave sleeps and she guards him, it is as if she is guarding her own courtyard. When he is awake, he guards himself, so it is not guarded through her.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard that is guarded with her awareness. Only this kind of courtyard acquires for her.

phrases.english: Rava says:
If he wrote a bill of divorce for her,
and placed it in the hand of her slave while he was sleeping,
and she is guarding him, it is a valid bill of divorce.
If he was awake, it is not a bill of divorce,
because he is like a courtyard
that is guarded without her awareness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כָּתַב לָהּ גֵּט, וּנְתָנוֹ בְּיַד עַבְדָּהּ יָשֵׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ברייתא discussion: giving a גט through the wife's slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט placed in the hand of a sleeping slave whom the wife guards is valid. If the slave is awake, it is not.

steps.title: But a slave is a walking courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: a slave is a 'walking courtyard,' and a walking courtyard cannot acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said that if he is sleeping and she guards him, it is a valid גט. Why? He is a walking courtyard, and a walking courtyard does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of רבא's ruling. It asks how a slave can acquire the גט for her at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a 'walking courtyard,' something that moves around, cannot acquire for its owner. A slave can move, so he should not count as her courtyard, even while he is asleep.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'walking courtyard,' a moving object, which cannot acquire for its owner

phrases.english: If he is sleeping and she is guarding him, it is a valid bill of divorce.
Why?
He is a mobile courtyard,
and a mobile courtyard does not acquire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the sleeping slave acquires the גט for her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave is a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard cannot acquire.

steps.title: Sleeping is not different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer, that a sleeping slave is not moving. רבא himself ruled that anything which cannot acquire while moving also cannot acquire while standing or sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that sleeping is different, didn't רבא himself say: anything that would not acquire if it were moving also does not acquire when it is standing or sitting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in advance a reply someone might give, and shows why that reply fails. The challenge to רבא is now even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say a sleeping slave is not moving right now, so he is not a 'walking courtyard.' But רבא's own rule says we go by what the thing is, not by what it is doing at the moment. Something that walks is a walking courtyard even while it stands still.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. It introduces a possible answer the גמרא is about to reject.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this step brings a new answer. It knocks down a possible answer, so רבא's ruling is still under attack.

phrases.english: And if you would say that sleeping is different,
but didn't Rava say:
Anything that would not acquire if it were moving,
also does not acquire when standing or sitting!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא יָשֵׁן שָׁאנֵי, וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects in advance an answer to the challenge in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible answer that a sleeping slave is different
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's own rule says that something which cannot acquire while moving also cannot acquire while still.

steps.title: רבא meant a slave who is tied up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבא's ruling applies only when the sleeping slave is tied up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: when the slave is tied up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by limiting רבא's ruling to a slave who is tied up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tied-up slave cannot move at all, so he is not a 'walking courtyard.' Asleep, tied, and guarded by her, he works like a courtyard she is guarding, and the גט is valid.
steps.whatToRemember: A slave normally counts as a 'walking courtyard' and cannot acquire a גט for his owner. רבא's ruling works only when the slave is tied up, asleep, and guarded by her.

phrases.english: And the halakha applies where he is bound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 29 and 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the ruling applies only to a tied-up slave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seemed to apply to any sleeping slave, which runs into the 'walking courtyard' problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to a slave who is tied up and cannot move.

steps.title: משנה: A גט thrown to her in a public area
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on a גט thrown to a woman in a public area. Closer to her, she is divorced. Closer to him, she is not. Exactly in between, it is a doubt. The same rules apply to קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was standing in a public area and he threw the גט to her: if it landed closer to her, she is divorced. If closer to him, she is not divorced. If exactly halfway, she is in doubt whether she is divorced or not. The same rules apply to קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens, about a husband who throws the גט to his wife in a public area that belongs to no one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a public area, neither of them owns the ground, so the question is who is closer to the גט. If it is closer to her, it counts as having reached her. If it is closer to him, it is still with him. Exactly in the middle, the case is left as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה. A new משנה starts here.
Public domain, an area no one owns

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If she was standing in the public domain
and he threw it to her,
if it is closer to her, she is divorced.
If it is closer to him, she is not divorced.
If it is exactly halfway,
she is divorced and not divorced.
phrases.notes: This means it is a doubt: we are not sure whether she is divorced.

phrases.english: And the same applies to betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה עוֹמֶדֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וּזְרָקוֹ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט thrown in a public area: closer to her, she is divorced. Closer to him, she is not. Exactly halfway, it is a doubt. The same applies to קידושין.

steps.title: The same throwing rules apply to paying back a debt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the throwing rules to a debt. If the money lands closer to the מלוה, he has acquired it. If it lands closer to the לוה, the לוה still owes. If it lands exactly in between, they split the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true for a debt. Suppose the lender told the borrower, 'Throw me my debt,' and he threw it. If it landed closer to the lender, the lender acquired it. If it landed closer to the borrower, the borrower is still obligated. If it landed exactly in between, the two of them split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from the גט and קידושין case and applies the same three-zone rule to a borrower throwing repayment money to a lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the lender asked for the money to be thrown, it counts as his once it lands in his zone. If it is lost after that, the loss is his and the borrower is free. If it lands in the borrower's zone, it is still the borrower's money and he still owes. In the doubtful middle case, each side carries half the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Creditor; the person who is owed money

steps.whatToRemember: The three zones (closer to her or him, closer to the other person, exactly in between) apply in the same way to a גט, to קידושין, and to repaying a debt.

phrases.english: And the same is true regarding a debt:
If his creditor said to him:
"Throw me my debt,"
and he threw it to him;
if it landed closer to the lender, the lender acquired it.
If it landed closer to the borrower, the borrower is still obligated.
If it was exactly halfway, the two of them split it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's throwing rules from גט and קידושין to repaying a debt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the money lands closer to the lender, he acquired it. If it lands closer to the borrower, the borrower still owes. If it lands exactly in between, they split the loss.

steps.title: What counts as 'closer to her' and 'closer to him'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the exact meaning of the משנה's terms 'closer to her' and 'closer to him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the case of 'closer to her,' and what is the case of 'closer to him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for a clear definition of the משנה's word 'closer.' This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Closer' is vague. Does it mean measured with a ruler, or something else? The גמרא wants a firm legal measure that decides when the גט counts as hers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the case of 'closer to her,'
and what is the case of 'closer to him'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the משנה's terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear definition of 'closer to her' and 'closer to him.'

steps.title: רב: 'closer' means within that person's four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'closer to her' means the גט landed within her ארבע אמות, and 'closer to him' means within his ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Within her four אמות is 'closer to her.' Within his four אמות is 'closer to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by tying 'closer' to the known halachic zone of ארבע אמות around each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The space of ארבע אמות around a person in a public area works like his own property, and it acquires for him. So the deciding test is whose zone the גט landed in, not simply measured distance.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits; the zone around a person that can acquire for him

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ – זֶהוּ קָרוֹב לָהּ,
phrases.english: Her four cubits: this is 'closer to her,'

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ – זֶהוּ קָרוֹב לוֹ.
phrases.english: his four cubits: this is 'closer to him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'closer.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Closer' means the item landed inside that person's ארבע אמות.

steps.title: What counts as 'exactly in between'?
steps.stepSummary: Now that 'closer' means each person's ארבע אמות, the גמרא asks how there can be a 'halfway' case at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'halfway'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה's 'exactly in between' case looks like. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person has his own ארבע אמות, the item seems to land either in one zone, in the other, or in neither. The גמרא wants to know when there is a real doubt between the two people.

keyTerms.meaning: Half and half; exactly in between

phrases.english: What is the case of 'halfway'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רב's definition by asking about the third case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real-life case of 'exactly in between.'

steps.title: Both people standing within the same four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק says 'halfway' means both people were standing within the same ארבע אמות, so the spot where the גט lands belongs to both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: For example, when both of them were standing within the same four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that the doubt happens when the two people stand so close together that their ארבע אמות overlap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גט lands in a spot that is inside both people's zones, we cannot tell whose zone acquired it. That is why the ruling is a doubt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
For example, when the two of them were standing
within the same four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן עוֹמְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what 'halfway' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Halfway means both people are standing within the same ארבע אמות.

steps.title: Whoever got there first should own the spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: we should check which person reached that area first, and the ארבע אמות should belong to that person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us see which of them came there first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'both in the same four אמות' explanation by saying there should be no doubt at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever arrived first already had those ארבע אמות as his zone, so the other person's arrival should not take it away. Then we would know whose zone it is, and the case would not be a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us see; let us check

phrases.english: But let us see which of them came first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of the 'halfway' case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק's definition of 'halfway' as both people standing within the same ארבע אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whoever arrived first owns the zone, so the case should be decided and not a doubt.

steps.title: Arriving at the exact same moment is impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer, that both people arrived at the same instant. It is impossible to be that exact, so one of them must have come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that both of them came at the same time, but it is impossible to be that exact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down one possible way out of the challenge, so the 'halfway' explanation of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק still has a problem. The next step drops that explanation and gives a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could answer that the two arrived together, so neither came first. The גמרא rejects this because two events never line up at exactly the same instant. So the challenge from the previous step still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)
It is impossible to be exactly precise

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question. It only removes one possible answer, so the challenge against the 'halfway' explanation still stands until רב כהנא gives a new explanation in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דַּאֲתוֹ תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: And if you would say that both of them came at the same time,
but it is impossible to be that exact!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דַּאֲתוֹ תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge by ruling out the 'simultaneous arrival' answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible answer that both people arrived together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is impossible for two arrivals to happen at exactly the same instant (אי אפשר לצמצם).

steps.title: רב כהנא: The case is exactly eight אמות apart
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives a new answer to how a 'halfway' case can exist. The couple stand exactly eight אמות apart, so each person's four אמות border the other's, and 'halfway' is the exact line between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב כהנא said: Here we are dealing with a case of exactly eight אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer was knocked down, so the גמרא brings a new answer from רב כהנא. 'Halfway' happens when the couple stand exactly eight אמות apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person owns the four אמות around them. If they stand exactly eight אמות apart, his area and her area touch with no gap and no overlap. A גט that lands right on the border line is not closer to either one, and that is the 'halfway' case. Because the areas do not overlap, the question of who arrived first (step 38) no longer comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It tells us the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
Eight אמות: his four plus her four.
Exact, precise. Not one bit more or less.
We are dealing with. It tells us what case the משנה is talking about.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב כהנא, 'halfway' means the couple stand exactly eight אמות apart. Their two areas touch, and the גט landed right on the line between them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'eight אמות' as a distance of four from each person to the גט with the areas overlapping. The point is that the two areas sit right next to each other, so there is no shared area to fight over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer gets around the problem from steps 38-39. Nobody needs to have 'arrived first' when the two areas never overlap.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Kahana said:
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means we drop the answer of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק, which was just knocked down.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with exactly eight cubits,
phrases.notes: His four אמות and her four אמות touch exactly, so the גט lands right on the line where they meet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The answer of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק was rejected in steps 38-39, so this step gives a new answer to the question from step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Halfway' is a case where the couple stand exactly eight אמות apart. Their four-אמות areas touch, and the גט falls on the border between them.
